problem:
The table below gives some values of a continuous function $f(x)$ on the closed interval $[-6,3].$ The right Riemann sum approximation to the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ with $3$ equal subintervals has a value of $6.$ What must be the value of $k?$

| $x$ | $-6$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $7$ | $5$ | $-2$ | $k$ |

feedback.problem: A right Riemann sum is used to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=-1$ and $x=1$ for each of the functions below. For which function does the Riemann sum give an *overestimate* of the area?
feedback.worked_solution:
The right Riemann sum overestimates the area under the respective curve if the function is increasing over the given interval. 

Of the given options, the only function that is increasing over $x\in [-1,1]$ is as follows.
